g_policy.reason: The offer copy states the one-hour Search reward before play, and the flow lets users choose the game. The decline and ad-failure fields leave the menu usable and withhold the reward if play is not verified.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward field offers time in Search, not cash or a transferable or externally exchangeable item.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger event is a return to the profile menu without subscribing; it does not require chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal says it removes nothing free, and its expiry field changes the menu card, not access to the existing Search tab.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is a card in the s09 profile menu, which the product model rates content safe, rather than in a conversation.

c1_revealed_value.reason: This is an existing_anchor, but the model shows neither a charge nor a limit for the Search access given by the one-hour reward; the observed Janitor+ benefits in m02 do not include Search.

c2_evidence.reason: The what-makes-it-work field claims Search finds characters by name and trait filters. The cited s05.e01 only says “Search”; no supplied element supports those existing capabilities.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The offered-to and subscribers fields restrict the card to free users and say subscribers never see it.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward expires after 60 minutes and does not grant the Janitor+ benefits listed in m02 or take an existing advantage from other users.

c5_moment.reason: The placement is a card in the persistent profile menu that the user chooses to open, not an interruption to an active task.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The flow uses a short sponsored game, the trigger is a detectable return to the profile menu, and the ad-failure field says unverified play does not turn on the reward.

c7_specific.reason: The proposal names the s09 Upgrade to Janitor Plus entry and the app’s Search tab as the trigger context and reward.

other_concern: An hour of Search may have no practical value if users can already use Search without a limit. The proposal does not say that free Search stops when the hour ends; if that is intended, it would change the free-removal verdict.
